sources.entry: HomeButler - Installs and manages a curated catalog of applications via Docker Compose, maps containers and exposed ports, verifies backups restore, and reports what changed since the last run with CLI, JSON, web and MCP interfaces. (Source Code) MIT Docker/Go

summary.one_liner: HomeButler is a single Go binary that snapshots a homelab server, reports what changed since the last run, and offers the same answers through a CLI, JSON output, a web dashboard, and an MCP server.
summary.what_it_does: It writes a health report that compares the current server state against the latest saved snapshot and classifies each change as gone, new, replaced, image, state, port, disk, or skipped. It can install a curated set of self-hosted apps via docker compose with pre-checks for Docker, ports, and duplicates. It maps containers, exposed ports, and topology through inventory scan, with Mermaid export. Backup drill boots a backup archive in an isolated container and requires an HTTP health check to pass. It also includes a doctor preflight check, a watch command that tracks container, systemd, and PM2 restarts with crash analysis, and Proxmox VE cluster status and guest power actions. It runs over SSH on remote machines and needs no daemon.
use_cases: detect what changed on a homelab server since last time
install self-hosted apps like Uptime Kuma or Jellyfin with docker compose
verify that a backup can actually be restored
find which container owns a port or which ports are exposed
give an AI assistant read-only access to server status
monitor container restarts and diagnose crash loops
check a Proxmox cluster's nodes and guests
notable: Change reports use a fixed kind word (gone, new, replaced, image, state, port, disk, skipped) that is shared between human output and --json, so agents can branch on it
backup drill boots backup archives in isolated Docker networks and fails non-zero when the health check fails
No daemon, no database, and no open ports by default; the web dashboard is opt-in and binds 127.0.0.1
MCP server supports a --max-risk read mode that hides tools that make changes
Web dashboard is embedded in the Go binary via go:embed
caveats: Power actions on Proxmox guests need a separate action token and an explicit --confirm flag
Restarting systemd services needs root or a polkit rule; flapping targets are intentionally not restarted
Building the web dashboard with make build-all requires Node; make build produces a CLI without it
keywords: check what changed on my server
